extracted.intended_audience: AI developers, data scientists, product/security/legal teams creating model documentation; also policymakers and nontechnical stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Create structured, transparent documentation for machine learning models (model cards), following NVIDIA's Model Card++ enhancements that emphasize bias, explainability, privacy, safety, and discoverability. Applicable to developers, product teams, and organizations publishing ML models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model metadata (version, type, date, license, publisher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards can also record model version, type, date, license restrictions, information about the publishing organization, and other qualitative information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit fields for model versioning and provenance so users can compare models and track updates; surface license restrictions clearly as respondents cited licensing information as a top priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended use and out-of-scope applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Information includes intended use cases and out-of-scope applications, expected users, and who developed the model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intended users and intended domains up front to help downstream decision-makers determine fitness-for-use; explicitly list out-of-scope scenarios where the model should not be applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery was noted as one area of improvement — model cards need to be located where interested individuals can reference them and be findable alongside models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish model cards in the same repository as models, make fields filterable/searchable, and promote them on platforms so both technical and nontechnical users can find and use them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, consistent, concise language and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: NVIDIA model cards aim to present AI models using clear, consistent, and concise language, and encourages using a consistent organizational structure, simple format, and clear language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a consistent schema/organization and plain-language explanations to make cards useful to nontechnical stakeholders, customers, students, and policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative performance metrics and KPIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards report quantitative evaluation metrics and key performance indicators; performance was highlighted as one of the most important areas users want to see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear metrics (aggregate and disaggregated) and define KPIs; place performance and licensing in dedicated sections for easy reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance across demographic groups and fairness metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about how the model performs with different demographic groups, including performance metrics for different demographic groups, is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose disaggregated evaluation results, document observed disparities, and use these results to inform model selection and mitigation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias mitigation — steps taken
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps taken to mitigate unwanted bias are documented in Model Card++; respondents wanted more information about datasets used to train and validate the model—particularly details regarding unwanted bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific mitigation measures (processes, algorithms, validations) and link them to observed metrics; document collaboration with bias assessment experts where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset provenance and traceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provenance of training datasets, including what type of data was collected and how it was collected, is a required disclosure in the ++ Promise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document dataset sources, collection methods, storage, traceability, and any dataset versioning. Include information sufficient to assess representativeness and potential gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset storage and quality validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Card++ describes dataset storage and quality validation as part of enhanced model card disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail where datasets are stored, retention policies, quality checks performed, and validation methods used to ensure data integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy disclosures and personal data use
rubrics_metrics.description: Key disclosures related to privacy and personal data use are part of Model Card++.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what personal data (if any) was used, legal bases, consent mechanisms, and any privacy-preserving measures (e.g., anonymization, differential privacy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety and security (technical limitations, known risks, potential impacts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical limitations, known risks, and potential safety impacts are explicitly disclosed in the Model Card++ subsections for Safety and Security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List known failure modes, worst-case scenarios, adversarial risks, and recommended mitigations or monitoring strategies for deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explainability (domains, decision logic, compliance review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Explainability subcard provides information about example domains for an AI model, intended users, decision logic, and compliance review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe model decision logic at an appropriate level of detail, examples of use domains, and results or status of any compliance or explainability reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should include limitations and ethical considerations to inform stakeholders about potential harms and appropriate use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document ethical trade-offs, known societal impacts, and recommendations for safe or restricted use; surface analysis used to reach these conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured schema and machine-readable fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards are structured and organized in schema and can communicate a common software quality expectation; adding filterable and searchable fields is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standardized schema with discrete fields (machine- and human-readable) so information can be programmatically indexed and compared across models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training methodology and development approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards provide information about the deep learning training methodology itself and NVIDIA includes the ++ Promise describing their software development approach to model development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include training procedures, hyperparameters (as appropriate), datasets used for training vs. validation, and the organization’s development practices relevant to trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative updates and regulatory alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: NVIDIA iteratively updates its model card documentation in alignment with evolving regulations, including global frameworks such as the EU AI Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to updating cards as models or regulations change; document revision history and how the card meets applicable regulatory transparency/safety requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery-promoting publication practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards should be discoverable — developers should be able to find and promote model cards alongside their work, whether in research papers or deployed models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish cards in model repositories, link them from papers and product pages, and adopt naming/placement conventions that increase visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-aware presentation (nontechnical and technical readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI model cards should not just be built for developers; companies should also build model cards that are accessible to nontechnical individuals and technical experts alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide layered explanations (high-level summaries + technical appendices) so both nontechnical stakeholders and experts can get appropriate levels of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tooling to automate and standardize cards
rubrics_metrics.description: NVIDIA supports processes and tools such as the Model Card Generator to automate and standardize documentation, simplifying the generation of model cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage automated extraction tools to populate standard fields from code and metadata, reducing friction and encouraging consistent adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with impacted stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Model cards are a best practice, encouraging developers to engage with the people who will ultimately be impacted by the model’s output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document stakeholder engagement activities (consultations, user studies) and how feedback influenced model design, evaluation, or mitigation strategies.
